edges.description: Severe structural osteopenia and brittle bone architecture cause congenital and recurrent postnatal fractures.
Markedly reduced cortical width and trabecular bone volume produce extremely low areal BMD Z-scores (-5 to -6).
Decreased bone modeling and recurrent fractures produce marked bowing and deformity of the long bones.
Vertebral fragility and whole-bone osteopenia lead to progressive scoliosis and kyphoscoliosis in survivors.
Extreme fragility of thin, osteopenic ribs results in multiple perinatal rib fractures.
Multiple rib fractures and thoracic cage fragility cause neonatal respiratory distress and perinatal respiratory failure.

nodes.description: Overmodified type I collagen assembles into fibrils with abnormal diameters and irregular borders, forming an abnormal bone extracellular matrix characterized by decreased cortical width, extremely thin trabeculae, and focal patches of unmineralized osteoid. nodes.description: P3H1 (LEPRE1) forms a 1:1:1 endoplasmic-reticulum complex with cartilage-associated protein (CRTAP) and cyclophilin B (CyPB/PPIB). Biallelic null P3H1 variants eliminate the protein and, because P3H1 and CRTAP mutually stabilize one another, also deplete CRTAP — collapsing the complex that both 3-hydroxylates collagen and delivers the CyPB folding chaperone to the nascent chain. The same complex underlies the closely related recessive OI types VII (CRTAP) and IX (PPIB).
